Data/Geometry.lua carries the value only in a header comment (line 13, 'single linkage at 100 yd'), no field. QuestieSource's copy must equal the generator's: Hub() re-implements nearest_hub's LINK-yard cell grid over the townAnchors the generator linked at LINK, so a changed generator value silently mis-assigns hubs. The Integrations and Model copies are tolerances defined as 'the town linkage' by their own comments, so they are meant to follow it too.
items.reason: Unify these copies behind one helper in a reviewed refactor? The copies differ in small ways, so the shared helper is a design choice, not a mechanical move.

items.quote: local private = zoneDB and zoneDB["private"]
items.what: `zoneDB and` cannot be false when Support.Get returns nil: the previous line ends in `or {}`; either drop the `and` or drop the `or {}`, one guard is enough.
items.why: Integrations/QuestieSource.lua:94 is `local zoneDB = type(lib.Support) == "table" and lib.Support.Get("ZoneDB") or {}`, so a nil or false answer is already replaced by a table and the following `type(private) ~= "table"` check returns QUESTIE_ZONES. The two guards cover the same missing-ZoneDB case twice.

items.quote: elseif ns.Data == empty then
items.what: A finished build whose ns.Data is no longer the `empty` placeholder is dropped with no else branch, leaving status.state at "building" (set at line 399); settle the status in an else branch, or drop the condition if nothing can swap ns.Data.
items.why: rg 'ns\.Data = ' outside tests finds only Data/Geometry.lua:49 (load time) and lines 374 and 412 of this file, so the condition is false only when Start runs a second time (Questie.API.RegisterOnReady(Start) at line 422 calling back again). In that case Start has already set status.state = "building" and Step neither swaps nor resets it, so ns.QuestieBuilding() (Core/Core.lua:692-698, `state == "building"`) stays true: Rebuild and StepRebuild hold the route for good and ns.SourceHint keeps showing the loading line, with nothing printed. Whether Questie ever calls the ready callback twice is not established from this repository, hence low confidence.
items.reason: A second completed Start would leave status.state at building after the identity check fails, and Core.QuestieBuilding would continue blocking rebuilds. However, the repository and in-flight branch do not establish that RegisterOnReady invokes a registered callback repeatedly; its host contract or implementation is needed.

items.quote: result.source = ADDON .. " " .. version
items.what: The `source` field QuestieSource writes onto ns.Data (here and `empty.source = "QuestieDB unavailable"` on line 373) is fully dead: nothing reads it, so delete both writes (and the stale `---@field source string where the data came from, for /agf audit` in types/Namespace.lua, or have Audit print it).
items.why: `rg '\.source\b'` over all *.lua/*.py (tests, tools, UI, Core included) returns only these two writes plus an unrelated `reagent.source` in UI/WindowProfessions.lua; `rg '"source"|data\.source|Data\.source'` returns nothing. Core/Core.lua Audit() prints `data.build` and reports the source from ns.QuestieStatus.state/version/reason instead, and UI/Dump.lua saves ns.QuestieStatus, not ns.Data. Paths checked: dynamic (the only string-keyed walk is `for key, value in pairs(bundled)` copies, not a reader), public surface (ns.Data is not a cross-addon API), manifests/docs (no mention), data-driven (not persisted to SavedVariables), cross-boundary (generated Data/Geometry.lua also writes `source`, outside this slice), open work: `git grep 'Data\.source'` on remote branches finds readers only in tests/questie_spec.lua of old cb/b2-*/b3-* branches (`h.ns.Data.source:find("^CMaNGOS")`), assertions the current spec no longer has.
